text: Agathelos the Raging. Agathelos the Raging is a colossal armored boar penned within the thorned tunnels of Razorfen Kraul. Reared by the Death's Head quilboar as a living siege engine and avatar of their ancient god, he has been driven into a violent, unnatural frenzy. His sheer mass and strength make him one of the most dangerous beasts lurking under the Southern Barrens. Quilboar venerate all swine as descendants of their patron deity and progenitor, the god Agamaggan. To them, boars of exceptional size and tenacity are considered direct blessings from their fallen god. A beast the size of Agathelos—standing roughly twice as tall as a Barrens thunder lizard—carries massive spiritual and ceremonial significance among the Razorfen tribes.

Aggem Thorncurse. Aggem Thorncurse is a spectral quilboar encountered deep within the thorned tunnels of Razorfen Kraul. Bound beyond death to the service of his tribe, he fights alongside Warlord Ramtusk and Death Speaker Jargba to defend their sacred redoubt against intruders. Within the heart of Razorfen Kraul, the quilboar fight desperately to protect their ancestral dens from outsiders. Aggem Thorncurse is not among the living defenders; instead, he lingers as a restless spirit. Bound to the physical realm by dark geomancy and shamanic rites, Aggem takes up arms when intruders threaten the tribe's warlord.

Aku'mai. Aku'mai is a monstrous, three-headed hydra dwelling in the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps along the Zoram Strand. Imbued with primordial shadow and favored by the ancient Old Gods, the beast is revered as a herald of apocalyptic ruin. The Twilight's Hammer cult tends to the creature in its submerged lair, offering living sacrifices to sate its eternal hunger. Long before cultists claimed the sunken temple beneath the sea, Aku'mai haunted the coast of Ashenvale as a living blight upon the Zoram Strand. A creature of deep water and darker powers, this gargantuan hydra carries a fragment of the Old Gods' ancient malevolence within its three ravenous heads. Rather than an ordinary denizen of the tides, Aku'mai is an ancient terror that has lurked in the submerged ruins since the fall of the night elves' temple to Elune, poisoning the waters with Void-tainted malice.

Arcanist Doan. Arcanist Doan is a master human mage residing within the Athenaeum of the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing. Formerly an associate of the Silver Hand who assisted in forging the legendary Ashbringer, he now serves the Scarlet Crusade as one of its most lethal arcane specialists and guardian of key crusade archives. Before the Scarlet Crusade turned inward and zealous, Arcanist Doan walked among the Knights of the Silver Hand. During the Third War, he met with Highlord Alexandros Mograine and other founders at Southshore. When Mograine revealed a shadowy crystal taken from an orc warlock during the Second War, Doan observed its unnatural ability to absorb holy energy. Joining his arcane insight with the holy magic of his peers, Doan helped cleanse the void crystal into radiant light, forming the heart of the weapon known as the Ashbringer.

Baron Aquanis. Baron Aquanis is a powerful water elemental of the flooded Moonshrine Ruins in Blackfathom Deeps, where the Twilight's Hammer has made its lair. He rises from the deep water when someone disturbs the ruins' Fathom Stone. The shamans of the Earthen Ring have long thought him a corrupted elemental power, and they suspect the cult is behind it. Submerged beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Stone lies right under the noses of the Twilight's Hammer cultists who now occupy the ruins. Inside it is a fathom core, a device that, properly read, tells the history of all elemental activity around it. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover the core, and disturbing the stone draws Baron Aquanis up from the depths.

Baron Silverlaine. Baron Silverlaine was the rightful human lord of the fortress once known as Keep Silverlaine, perched high above Pyrewood Village. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the savage worgen upon the region, the baron and his household were mercilessly slaughtered. Now, his tormented spirit lingers in the ruined dining hall, bound in undeath to defend the very lair that became his tomb. Before the shadow of the wolf-beasts blanketed the southern hills of Silverpine, Baron Silverlaine ruled over a proud noble estate. His fortress provided safety and oversight to the surrounding Gilnean lands. That peace shattered when Archmage Arugal, seeking a weapon against the rampaging Scourge, unleashed summoned worgen into the region. The feral monstrosities could not be controlled; they stormed the stronghold, overran its guards, and butchered the baron along with his entire family.

Bazil Thredd. Bazil Thredd is Edwin VanCleef's lieutenant and most trusted assistant, locked in the Stormwind Stockade since the Stonemasons' riots that killed Queen Tiffin. Now the prison has risen in revolt, and Thredd leads the rioting Defias inmates from its eastern cell block. When the Stonemasons Guild was refused payment by the nobility of Stormwind for rebuilding the city, Edwin VanCleef rejected government appeasements and sparked open revolt. Bazil Thredd stood at VanCleef's side as his chief lieutenant and most trusted assistant. During the violent clashes that followed—which resulted in the death of Queen Tiffin Wrynn—Thredd was captured by the city guard. While VanCleef and the surviving masons fled into Westfall to form the Defias Brotherhood, Thredd was cast into the depths of the Stormwind Stockade.

Bazzalan. Bazzalan is a sinister satyr rogue lurking within the volcanic depths of Ragefire Chasm. Alongside Jergosh the Invoker, he commands the dark activities of the Searing Blade cult directly beneath the Horde capital of Orgrimmar. While Thrall works to establish the Orcs' new home across Durotar, ancient evils have found a roost beneath his feet. Bazzalan, a cunning satyr rogue, has allied with the Searing Blade cult inside the winding lava caverns of Ragefire Chasm. Swift and lethal with twin blades, he serves as one of the cult's primary field commanders.

Blind Hunter. The Blind Hunter is an elusive, albino bat that roosts deep within Razorfen Kraul. Unlike the ordinary bats nesting near the cavern entrances, this rare creature prowls the sunless depths of the quilboar redoubt. Razorfen Kraul is riddled with winding briars and dark subterranean caverns. While common Kraul bats roost nearer to the surface where faint light filters in from the outside world, the Blind Hunter has adapted entirely to the furthest, darkest alcoves of the tangle. Its pale, albino hide and milky gaze are likely the result of generations spent completely isolated from natural sunlight.

Bloodmage Thalnos. Bloodmage Thalnos is a skeletal spellcaster who haunts the Graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Once a sadistic interrogator within the Scarlet Crusade, he succumbed to the plague of undeath he fanatically fought against, yet he remains entrenched deep within their holy grounds. Within the zealous ranks of the Scarlet Crusade, Thalnos earned dark notoriety for his brutal methods of torture, used under the guise of purifying prospective recruits of taint. Yet despite his fanatical devotion to rooting out corruption, the sadistic mage ultimately succumbed to the plague of undeath. Rather than being cleansed or permanently destroyed, he rose as a withered skeleton, still clinging to his fiery magic and arcane mastery.

Bruegal Ironknuckle. Bruegal Ironknuckle is an infamous dwarven prisoner held within the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the petty criminals and rioting rabble that fill the holding cells, he is a formidable brawler whose presence deep inside the corridors spells immediate danger to anyone trying to restore order. When the Stormwind Stockade erupted into open revolt, many of the city's most volatile cutthroats took control of the subterranean cellblocks. Among them is Bruegal Ironknuckle, a particularly dangerous dwarf inmate known for brutal brawling strength. Rather than staying confined to a single cell, he prowls the riot-torn hallways, ready to bash anyone attempting to quell the uprising.

Captain Greenskin. Captain Greenskin is an elite goblin pirate overseeing the construction and crew of Edwin VanCleef's massive ironclad juggernaut. Hidden deep in the subterranean cove of the Deadmines, he commands the pirate forces hired by the Defias Brotherhood. His goal is to bring the warship to readiness to sail against Stormwind. Pacing the main deck of the gigantic juggernaut under construction in the Deadmines cove, Captain Greenskin represents the naval backbone of the Defias conspiracy. A seasoned goblin mariner who previously operated out of Booty Bay, Greenskin was brought into Edwin VanCleef's inner circle to turn an underground cavern into a drydock for an engine of war.

Charlga Razorflank. Charlga Razorflank, widely known as the Crone of the Kraul, is the fierce and cunning geomancer chieftain presiding over Razorfen Kraul. Under her leadership, the Razorfen quilboar drove the tauren out of the southern Barrens through ruthless expansion. Within the tangled, massive brambles of Razorfen Kraul rules Charlga Razorflank. Revered by her people as a master geomancer whose experimental magic remains unmatched among quilboar, Charlga organized her fractious kin into a unified, lethal threat. She harnessed the primal earth and giant thorns sprouting from the demigod Agamaggan's remains, reshaping the labyrinthine Kraul into an impenetrable fortress.

Commander Springvale. Commander Springvale was once a devoted paladin and the head of Baron Silverlaine's armed guard at Shadowfang Keep. Slain alongside his men during the feral worgen slaughter orchestrated by Archmage Arugal, his vengeful spirit remains behind to haunt the castle halls. Even in death, his ghost fiercely guards the keep and seeks vengeance for his fallen master. Before the ruin of Shadowfang Keep, Commander Springvale stood as an honorable paladin dedicated to the Holy Light and a sworn defender of Baron Silverlaine. Leading the garrison in Silverpine Forest, he oversaw the keep's security during the fraught days following the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge.

Cookie. Cookie is an elite murloc serving as the ship's cook aboard the juggernaut hidden deep within the Deadmines. An unusual recruit among the Defias Brotherhood, he tends the crew's cauldrons beneath the watchful eye of Captain Greenskin and Edwin VanCleef. He is the only entirely optional boss encountered within the underground dry dock. Beneath the decks of the towering juggernaut in the Ironclad Cove, cooking duty falls neither to a human outrider nor a goblin engineer, but to a solitary murloc known simply as Cookie. How he secured the position remains a private secret kept by Edwin VanCleef himself. Whatever doubts the rest of the crew might harbor about a murloc presiding over their rations, pirates are rarely in a position to be picky, and in the underworld of Moonbrook, a meal is a meal.

Dark Iron Ambassador. Deep within the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan lurks the Dark Iron Ambassador, an elusive emissary sent by Emperor Dagran Thaurissan. His presence reveals that the fall of the gnome capital involves far more than just wild trogg incursions and madness. While Gnomeregan's catastrophic downfall is publicly blamed on the trogg invasion and High Tinker Mekkatorque's desperate radiation gambit, the presence of the Dark Iron Ambassador points to far darker machinations. Wandering the contaminated depths of the workshop corridors, this rare Dark Iron dwarf suggests that Sicco Thermaplugg did not betray his people in complete isolation.

Dextren Ward. Dextren Ward is an infamous criminal and grave robber locked away inside the Stormwind Stockade. Before his capture, he profited by exhuming bodies from Duskwood's Raven Hill Cemetery and delivering them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Now caught in the midst of the prison's bloody uprising, he remains marked for death by the town council of Darkshire. Before ending up in chains beneath the streets of Stormwind, Dextren Ward conducted a grim and lucrative business in the fog-choked woods of Duskwood. Raven Hill Cemetery was already a site of sorrow and growing horror, but Ward treated its burial grounds as a private quarry. Rather than hunting merely for trinkets and heirlooms left with the dead, Ward dealt in flesh, unearthing fresh graves to supply local dark practitioners.

Edwin VanCleef. Edwin VanCleef was the brilliant Guildmaster of the Stonemasons who rebuilt Stormwind City after the Second War. After being cheated of payment by the House of Nobles, he led a violent workers' revolt and formed the outlaw Defias Brotherhood. Operating from deep within the Deadmines of Westfall, he seeks vengeance against the kingdom he helped restore. Following the devastation of the First War, Edwin VanCleef was chosen to lead the Stonemasons Guild in the monumental task of rebuilding Stormwind City. A peerless craftsman and an idealist, VanCleef directed the construction of the capital's grand ramparts and towering cathedrals, and even oversaw the erection of Nethergarde Keep to watch over the Dark Portal. Alongside his mastery of architecture, VanCleef was a remarkably deadly operative; he was trained in stealth, subterfuge, and bladecraft by his childhood friend, Mathias Shaw.

Electrocutioner 6000. The Electrocutioner 6000 is a deadly, super-charged spider tank deployed to defend the Launch Bay within the irradiated halls of Gnomeregan. Piloted by the notorious leper gnome Lieutenant Tom 'Sizzlepants' Crankle, it represents Mekgineer Thermaplugg's reckless ambition to weaponize high-voltage electricity. Mekgineer Thermaplugg has never been known for rigorous safety testing. Driven by megalomania and haste, he regularly rushes unproven war machines straight from the drawing board into live combat. The Electrocutioner 6000 was his initial attempt to harness raw electrical currents as an offensive system mounted to an armored spider tank chassis. Rather than working out lethal power surges in a laboratory, Thermaplugg sent it immediately to guard the upper tiers of Gnomeregan's Launch Bay.

Fenrus the Devourer. Fenrus the Devourer is an enormous worg that prowls the upper sanctum of Shadowfang Keep. Kept as a personal pet and guardian by Archmage Arugal, the ravenous beast is bloated on unnatural magics. Anyone daring to breach the archmage's personal study must contend with this feral horror and the master who watches over it. Deep within Shadowfang Keep, just outside Archmage Arugal's personal chambers, lurks the monstrous worg known as Fenrus the Devourer. Unlike the lupine worgen roaming the ramparts, Fenrus is an actual worg, swollen to gargantuan proportions. Prowling the shelves, scrolls, and arcane apparatuses of Arugal's private study, the beast serves both as a pet and as a violent perimeter guard against any intruder seeking the mad mage's head.

Gelihast. Gelihast is a ferocious, twin-blade wielding murloc chieftain residing in the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps. Lured by the dark whispers of the Old Gods, he butchered his way into the sunken temple ruins before earning the reluctant respect of the Twilight's Hammer cultists. While most murlocs stay near coastal shallows, Gelihast felt the dark, ominous tug of the Old Gods deep beneath Ashenvale. Driven by these primordial whispers, he forced his way into the sunken temple of Blackfathom Deeps. When Twilight's Hammer cultists tried to halt his path, he slaughtered nearly a dozen of them single-handedly using his twin swords.

Ghamoo-ra. Ghamoo-ra is an ancient, giant sea turtle inhabiting the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps. Once a peaceful denizen of Elune's sunken temple, he was captured, tortured, and driven mad by the Twilight's Hammer cult to serve as a vicious guardian. Before the defilement of Blackfathom Deeps, Ghamoo-ra was among the last peaceful natural inhabitants dwelling among the flooded ruins of the night elven temple dedicated to Elune. When the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult took control of the sanctuary, they roused the ancient turtle from his quiet life and locked him in captivity. Rather than slain, he was systematically tormented for years, suffering mental and physical flaying at the hands of the cultists.

Gilnid. Gilnid, known as the Smelter, is the goblin master engineer running the forges in the depths of the Deadmines. He oversees the smelting of raw ore into refined metal and munitions for Edwin VanCleef's hidden ironclad juggernaut. Without his fiery operations, the Defias Brotherhood would lack the heavy cannons needed to assault Stormwind. Deep within the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood relies on industrial expertise to forge weapons of war. Gilnid serves as VanCleef's head smelter, commanding a small army of goblin laborers, tinkers, and smiths in the central foundry. Towering over most of his kin, he drives his crew relentlessly through smoke and slag, barking orders and refusing breaks to ensure raw iron ore is processed into heavy plating and lethal ordnance.

Hamhock. Hamhock is a massive two-headed ogre confined within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Locked away beneath the capital alongside hardened Defias insurgents and cutthroats, he looms as a particularly brutal and unexpected inmate amidst the prison riot. The Stormwind Stockade was built to hold petty thieves, murderers, and political dissidents, making a towering two-headed ogre an imposing sight among the cells. When the prisoners rose up and took control of the facility, Hamhock remained entrenched in the chaos, crushing anyone foolish enough to intrude on his cellblock.

Herod. Herod is a renowned champion and berserker of the Scarlet Crusade, commanding the Armory within the Scarlet Monastery. Known for his ferocious martial prowess and unyielding zeal, he trains recruits in the brutal melee combat needed to wage holy war. His death is sought by both Alliance dissidents and the Horde's rulers in Undercity to weaken the Crusade's military core. Within the fortified halls of the Scarlet Monastery's Armory, Herod stands as the embodiment of the Crusade's martial aggression. Unlike the spellcasters and paladins who channel holy magic in the Cathedral, Herod relies on raw, bloodthirsty physical power. Clad in mail and wielding a massive two-handed axe, he personally trains cohorts of Scarlet Trainees, instilling a furious devotion to exterminating anyone not allied with their fanatical cause.

High Inquisitor Fairbanks. High Inquisitor Fairbanks was once a revered priest of the Knights of the Silver Hand and the most trusted advisor to Highlord Alexandros Mograine. Betrayed, executed, and hidden away behind a secret door in the Scarlet Monastery Cathedral, his rotting, undead form stands as a grim monument to the Scarlet Crusade's dark descent. Before the fall of Lordaeron, Fairbanks was a respected holy man among the Knights of the Silver Hand. When Highlord Alexandros Mograine convened a fateful gathering at the Southshore inn, Fairbanks stood beside him, helping channel holy power into the enigmatic crystal that would eventually become the heart of the legendary Ashbringer. When Prince Arthas dissolved the paladin order, Fairbanks accompanied Mograine to Ironforge, standing witness as King Magni Bronzebeard forged the great blade to combat the Scourge.

Houndmaster Loksey. Houndmaster Loksey is the officer charged with breeding and training the fearsome war dogs of the Scarlet Crusade. Stationed in the kennels within the Scarlet Monastery's Armory, he directs packs of hounds to hunt down undead, intruders, and perceived heretics. His merciless discipline has made the Monastery's beasts infamous throughout Tirisfal Glades. Within the heavily fortified walls of the Scarlet Monastery, Houndmaster Loksey commands the training of vicious tracking and attack dogs. The Scarlet Crusade relies on these trained hounds to sniff out plague-tainted corpses, uncover hidden infiltrators, and run down any survivors fleeing the zealots' wrath. Loksey holds absolute authority over the Armory's kennel wing, ensuring his charges are primed to tear intruders apart limb by limb.

Interrogator Vishas. Interrogator James Vishas is the Scarlet Crusade's master of torment, stationed deep within the Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard wing. Infamous for his shrill voice and sheer cruelty, he takes twisted pleasure in breaking captives and testing the limits of mortal flesh. Few who enter his torture chambers ever leave with their minds or bodies intact. Within the dark crypts and burial grounds of the Scarlet Monastery, Interrogator Vishas tends to the Crusade's captive enemies. While the zealots outside march in gleaming armor under banners of purity, Vishas represents the grim reality behind their crusade: unbridled sadism cloaked in religious righteous fury. He approaches interrogation not merely as an intelligence duty, but as a prized craft, reveling in the agony of Forsaken captives, captured Scourge, and any living travelers unlucky enough to be branded heretics.

Jergosh the Invoker. Jergosh the Invoker is a treacherous orc warlock hiding deep within Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. As a high-ranking leader among the Searing Blade cultists, he practices demonic arts directly under the Warchief's nose and plots against the Horde. While Thrall works tirelessly to lead the orcs along a path of honor and shamanism, Jergosh rejected these ideals in favor of raw demonic power. Concealing himself within the subterranean labyrinth of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, he gathered followers into the Searing Blade, an insidious sect aligned with the remnants of the Shadow Council. Operating in the shadows directly below the Horde capital, Jergosh works to undo everything the new Horde stands for.

Kam Deepfury. Kam Deepfury is a notorious Dark Iron saboteur incarcerated within the depths of the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the majority of the prison's inmates, he has no allegiance to the Defias Brotherhood, having been captured for orchestrating a devastating explosion along the Thandol Span far to the north. While the Stockade is overwhelmingly filled with disgruntled Stonemasons and Defias rebels, Kam Deepfury stands apart. A Dark Iron dwarf of cunning and violence, Deepfury was captured and brought to Stormwind after masterminding an operation that crippled vital northern infrastructure. He is locked deep within the prison's cells, isolated from his kin beneath Blackrock Mountain but just as hostile to the Alliance as any rebel rioter sharing the corridors.

Lady Anacondra. Lady Anacondra is one of the Fanglords leading the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once a night elf acolyte named Scarletleaf, she was the first to volunteer for Naralex's ambitious effort to heal the Barrens. When her master's Emerald Dream communion turned into a nightmare, her mind broke, twisting her devotion into a venomous drive to see Kalimdor overrun by serpents. Before adopting her serpentine title, Lady Anacondra was known as Scarletleaf. When the elder druid Naralex conceived of tapping into the subterranean springs of the Barrens through the Emerald Dream, she stepped forward as his very first volunteer. Her eager loyalty, however, proved her undoing. As Naralex's mind was seized by dark visions, the nightmare seeped out from the dreaming realm and contaminated his disciples, shattering Scarletleaf's sanity and reshaping her reverie into a cold, reptilian obsession.

Lady Sarevess. Lady Sarevess is a twisted naga sorceress dwelling within the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. Allied with the Twilight's Hammer cultists who occupy the sunken temple, she experiments with dark sorceries in exchange for fresh sacrifices. Within the Pool of Ask'ar, Lady Sarevess conducts her rituals undisturbed in a private grotto provided by the Twilight's Hammer. The doomsday cultists supply her with a steady stream of living sacrifices, hoping her twisted magical research will yield a ward potent enough to protect them from the monstrous hydra they revere deeper in the cavern.

Lord Cobrahn. Lord Cobrahn, formerly the night elf druid Jarlaxla, is one of the corrupted Druids of the Fang lurking deep within the Wailing Caverns. Once renowned within the Cenarion Circle for his mastery of shapeshifting, he succumbed to the nightmare infecting the cavern springs. Renaming himself after his new lethal guise, Cobrahn now commands broods of deviate serpents and defends the twisted labyrinth. Before adopting the moniker Lord Cobrahn, Jarlaxla was a respected member of the Cenarion Circle, celebrated among his fellow druids for his extraordinary skill in channeling animal forms. When Naralex ventured into the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens hoping to tap their underground springs and restore lush life to the arid wastes, Jarlaxla accompanied him. However, when Naralex's Emerald Dream communion decayed into a twisting nightmare, Jarlaxla's mind shattered alongside his brothers.

Lord Pythas. Lord Pythas, once a night elf warrior named Aryn, is one of the four corrupted leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. Originally a childhood friend and sworn protector of the archdruid Naralex, he fell victim to the nightmare tainting the oasis underground. Now he wields both martial might and twisted serpent magic against any who try to reach his slumbering master. Before adopting the moniker Pythas, this night elf was known as Aryn. A seasoned warrior and trusted childhood companion to Naralex, he served as the archdruid's personal guard when the expedition ventured into the dry wastes of the Barrens. Eager to better serve Naralex's ambitious dream of restoring lush life to the arid realm, Aryn took up the study of druidism, proving to be an exceptionally fast learner. However, physical discipline and martial valor offered no shelter against the insidious corruption waiting deep within the subterranean fissures.

Lord Serpentis. Lord Serpentis is a corrupted night elf druid who stands as the supreme leader of the rogue Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once the most promising disciple of the master druid Naralex, his lofty ambition twisted into madness when the Emerald Nightmare took hold of the subterranean springs. Now, he commands the serpent-worshipping sect and aggressively protects the slumbering teacher he failed to emulate. Before darkness overtook the cavern springs, Serpentis was revered as Naralex's finest and most capable apprentice. He possessed exceptional power and prestige among the Cenarion circle, driven primarily by an ambition to become an honored teacher—a shan'do—in his own right. However, when Naralex attempted to tap the subterranean water beneath the Barrens and fell prey to a corrupting nightmare, Serpentis's pride and ambition left his mind vulnerable to the emerging madness.

Lorgus Jett. Lorgus Jett is a human member of the Twilight's Hammer cult operating within the flooded corridors of Blackfathom Deeps. Wandering the Moonshrine Ruins, he serves as a ruthless commander in the cult's service to the Old Gods. Horde leaders have singled him out as a primary target to disrupt the cult's encroaching presence along the Ashenvale coast. While many members of the Twilight's Hammer working under Blackfathom Deeps hail from orcish or tauren lineages, Lorgus Jett stands out as a human in the deep recesses of ancient night elf ruins. Roaming anywhere between the upper Moonshrine Ruins and the cavernous tunnels beyond the murloc defiler Gelihast, Jett coordinates the cult's dark rituals and violent ambitions.

Miner Johnson. Miner Johnson is an elusive, seasoned miner affiliated with the Defias Brotherhood deep inside the Deadmines. Tucked away in a side alcove alongside ordinary laborers, this dangerous prospector oversees excavation efforts ahead of the heavy machinery found deeper underground. Because he wanders the subterranean tunnels erratically, adventurers only occasionally cross his path. While hundreds of laborers pick at the subterranean veins of the Deadmines to supply Edwin VanCleef's hidden fortress, Miner Johnson stands out as an unusually formidable figure among them. Lurking in a shadowed alcove to the left before the lumbering shredders of the Mast Room, he is far tougher and more aggressive than the regular workforce. His unpredictable presence makes him a legendary target for explorers traversing the Defias tunnels.

Mr. Smite. Mr. Smite is the imposing tauren first mate serving aboard the Defias Brotherhood's flagship deep inside the Deadmines. An expert weaponmaster under Captain Greenskin, he commands the dockside approach to the hidden juggernaut with ruthless discipline. Intruders who face him must contend with his shifting arsenal and devastating physical strength. Guarding the docks of Ironclad Cove, Mr. Smite serves as first mate to the goblin Captain Greenskin. While the Defias Brotherhood is predominantly composed of disenfranchised humans and allied goblin tinkerers, Smite stands as a striking anomaly: a massive, battle-hardened tauren far from the plains of Kalimdor. Tasked with maintaining strict order among a rowdy pirate crew, he ensures that the labor fitting out Edwin VanCleef's secret dreadnaught proceeds without disruption.

Mutanus the Devourer. Mutanus the Devourer is a monstrous, pale murloc manifested directly from the Emerald Nightmare. Lurking in the darkest recesses of the sleeping druid Naralex's mind, it emerges to devour anyone attempting to break the Nightmare's hold over the Wailing Caverns. Slaying this twisted aberration is the final step in freeing Naralex from his tormented slumber. When the night elf druid Naralex tapped into the underground springs beneath the Barrens, he aimed to restore life to the arid wastes by connecting them to the Emerald Dream. Instead, an ancient corruption known as the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts. Trapped in an agonizing vision, Naralex's subconscious fears took physical form. The corruption seized upon a bizarre, primal revulsion in the druid's psyche—his deep-seated terror of murlocs—and amplified it into an immense, albino predator.

Naralex. Naralex is a night elf druid who sought to restore the parched Barrens to a lush forest using the powers of the Emerald Dream. Instead, his slumber was overtaken by a dark nightmare, twisting the Wailing Caverns beneath the earth and turning his followers into venomous fiends. Long before the Great Sundering, the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens were once a vibrant forest. Viewing this loss as a tragedy, Naralex journeyed south from Darnassus with a cohort of devoted disciples to reverse the drought. Deep beneath the savannah, he discovered an intricate subterranean network of underground springs and rushing geysers, naming them the Wailing Caverns after the howling wind and steam that moaned through the rock. He believed that by entering a deep trance and channeling the pristine energies of the Emerald Dream into these subterranean waters, the life-giving flow would reach the surface and cause the entire wasteland to bloom.

Oggleflint. Oggleflint is the chieftain of the trogg tribe dwelling within the volcanic depths of Ragefire Chasm directly beneath Orgrimmar. Once master of the entire subterranean cavern, he and his kin have been pushed toward the upper tunnels by the arrival of the Searing Blade cultists. Now entrenched near the entrance, he commands his savage pack and poses an immediate threat to the Horde capital above. Before shadow cultists infiltrated the chasm beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint and his troggs ruled the fiery subterranean tunnels uncontested. Brutal and territorial, they carved out a primitive domain among the molten rock. Though troggs possess little in the way of advanced civilization, Oggleflint maintained absolute authority over the pack through sheer brute strength.

Old Serra'kis. Old Serra'kis is an ancient, massive threshadon dwelling in the submerged subterranean waters of Blackfathom Deeps. While the invading Twilight's Hammer culled much of the temple's aquatic life for provisions, this enormous beast proved entirely lethal to any who attempted to hunt it. When the Twilight's Hammer cultists descended upon the sunken Moonshrine Ruins, they slaughtered the native wildlife beneath the waters for sustenance. Yet beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum, one primeval creature refused to become prey. Old Serra'kis, the largest threshadon in the sunken temple, made short work of any cultist brazen enough to spear him. Eventually, the hunters abandoned their efforts, leaving the ancient carnivore undisturbed in his watery domain.

Overlord Ramtusk. Overlord Ramtusk is the grizzled commander of the Death's Head tribe's military forces deep within Razorfen Kraul. A massive, aging quilboar warrior, his hide is heavily scarred from decades of brutal clashes across the Barrens. Striking him down shatters the martial backbone of the Kraul's defenders. Overlord Ramtusk has survived decades in one of Kalimdor's most violent frontiers. His thick, leathery hide is crisscrossed with deep scars earned in skirmishes against centaur raiding parties, feral harpies, encroaching orcs, and stalwart tauren braves. While advanced age slows many warriors, Ramtusk's seasoned instincts and physical resilience have only hardened, allowing him to rule Razorfen Kraul's standing garrison with unyielding authority.

Rhahk'Zor. Rhahk'Zor is a hulking ogre serving as the head foreman within the Deadmines. Overseeing Edwin VanCleef's subterranean construction efforts, he keeps the Defias laborers and miners in line through sheer brute force and heavy-handed discipline. Deep beneath the rolling hills of Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood has transformed the abandoned gold mines of Moonbrook into an underground fortress. Coordinating this sprawling construction requires harsh discipline, a role filled by the ogre Rhahk'Zor. Appointed as head foreman, he oversees the excavation crews and laborers, driving them forward to carve out tunnels and assemble VanCleef's secret projects.

Scarlet Commander Mograine. Scarlet Commander Mograine serves as the military leader garrisoned inside the Cathedral of the Scarlet Monastery. A zealous paladin of the Scarlet Crusade, he defends the chapel alongside High Inquisitor Whitemane. Both the Horde and Alliance target him to disrupt the zealots threatening Tirisfal Glades and the surrounding lands. Stationed within the grand Crusader's Chapel at the heart of the Scarlet Monastery, Scarlet Commander Mograine commands the standing garrison of the Scarlet Crusade. He wields the holy power of a paladin with ferocious dedication, relying on retribution, divine shields, and stunning blows to shatter any whom the Crusade deems corrupted or unclean.

Sneed. Sneed is the Defias Brotherhood's goblin lumbermaster stationed deep within the Deadmines. Operating from the lumber chamber known as the Mast Room, he pilots a heavy shredder of his own design to process timber for Edwin VanCleef's secret juggernaut. While the Defias Brotherhood draws its core membership from disenfranchised human stonemasons and common laborers, building an ironclad warship requires specialist trades. Edwin VanCleef recruited Sneed specifically for his engineering know-how and ruthless goblin efficiency. Stationed in the Mast Room along the subterranean rail network, Sneed oversees the rapid felling, cutting, and shaping of timber needed to frame VanCleef's colossal dreadnaught.

Sneed's Shredder. Sneed's Shredder is an imposing mechanised lumber harvester stationed deep within the Deadmines. Piloted by the goblin taskmaster Sneed, this deadly machine acts as both heavy industrial machinery for Edwin VanCleef's shipwrights and a terrifying perimeter defender. Within the goblin-dominated foundry of the Deadmines, mechanical shredders serve a dual purpose: processing vast amounts of timber and lumber required for Edwin VanCleef's hidden juggernaut, and serving as armored shock engines against intruders. Sneed, the overseer of the lumber works, operates this modified mechanical beast directly, turning an oversized buzzsaw into an instrument of defense.

Taragaman the Hungerer. Taragaman the Hungerer is a hulking felguard lurking within the molten caverns of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. While widely feared as the demonic master behind the Searing Blade cult, his presence in the fiery depths serves a darker, more deceptive purpose. The Horde seeks his destruction to eliminate the demonic taint poisoning the city's underbelly. Prowling amidst the magma pools of Ragefire Chasm, Taragaman the Hungerer represents an immediate and terrifying threat to the safety of Orgrimmar. For many scouts and young warriors sent into the dark chasm, the demonic felguard appears to be the central ringleader of the Searing Blade cultists, wielding infernal strength to bend the weak-willed and corrupt the subterranean passages beneath Thrall's fortress.

Targorr the Dread. Targorr the Dread is an infamous Blackrock orc executioner imprisoned deep within the Stormwind Stockade. Known for his brutal tortures of captured Stormwind soldiers, his execution was indefinitely delayed by bureaucratic incompetence and corruption. When the Stockade erupted into revolt under the Defias Brotherhood, Targorr broke free and allied with the rioting convicts. Before his capture, Targorr the Dread served as the supreme executioner for the Blackrock clan under Warlord Gath'Ilzogg. Operating out of the occupied ruins in Redridge, his cruelty stood out as exceptionally savage even by the violent standards of the Dark Horde. Stormwind guards and militiamen who fought to defend the borderlands were subjected to agonizing torment and slow death at his hands, making his name one of the most reviled in the kingdom.

Twilight Lord Kelris. Twilight Lord Kelris is an orc warlock and high-ranking leader within the Twilight's Hammer cult operating deep inside Blackfathom Deeps. From his perch in the Moonshrine Sanctum, he leads dark rituals and tends to the primordial hydra Aku'mai, aiming to usher in a reign of cosmic chaos. Twilight Lord Kelris directs the cultists of the Twilight's Hammer who seized the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. For years, Kelris slipped through the grasp of watchful eyes in Darnassus, evading the Argent Dawn and earning a grim reputation: whenever ancient malice stirred across Kalimdor, Kelris was suspected of orchestrating it. Rather than serving warlords or clans, this orc has pledged himself entirely to the Old Gods, seeking to unmake mortal civilization and return Azeroth to a state of absolute, primordial chaos.

Verdan the Everliving. Verdan the Everliving is a colossal bog beast lurking deep within the verdant tunnels of the Wailing Caverns. Once a peaceful protector of the underground springs and flora, he was twisted by the waking nightmare radiating from the sleeping druid Naralex. Now bound to the corrupted Druids of the Fang, Verdan violently attacks any who venture into his damp hollows. Long before Naralex arrived to tap into the natural springs of the Barrens, Verdan was formed from the overgrown foliage, silt, and moisture filling the caves. Thought to be the original guardian spirit of the subterranean oasis, Verdan was an ancient, gentle elemental keeping watch over the underground flora.

Viscous Fallout. Viscous Fallout is a corrupted water elemental wandering the irradiated corridors of Gnomeregan. Once a pure spirit inhabiting the city's pristine aquifers, it was twisted into a toxic monstrosity by Mekgineer Thermaplugg's devastating radiation release. Before the fall of Gnomeregan, the gnomish capital relied on sophisticated, intricate waterways and clean subterranean aquifers to power and sustain its mechanical marvels. A solitary water elemental dwelt peacefully within this pristine water supply. When the radiation vents were opened on Mekgineer Thermaplugg's treacherous advice to wipe out the invading troggs, the resulting chemical contamination seeped deep into the city's reservoirs, trapping the elemental and corrupting its very substance.

Camp Narache. Camp Narache is a secluded village nestled upon Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. It serves as the ancestral home of the Hawkwind tribe and the proving ground where young tauren begin their training. Sheltered high above the plains, the camp maintains ancient traditions while constantly guarding against encroaching quilboar and lingering centaur threats. Situated at the northern edge of the elevated Red Cloud Mesa, Camp Narache is the primary settlement of the Hawkwind tribe. The village consists of several large hide lodges and pavilions, including a communal tent for wounded braves, an armory, a bakery tent, and a spirit lounge dedicated to meditation and ancestral communion. At the center of the camp, tribal elders and path trainers stand in a circle at the heart of the camp, where the venerable Greatmother Hawkwind still offers guidance, guiding newly initiated youth as they step into their roles as defenders of the Earth Mother.

Camp Narache is the starting village for young tauren, located atop Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. It is the central encampment of the Hawkwind tribe, serving as a sanctuary where fledgling hunters, warriors, druids, and shamans master their crafts before traveling outward to Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff.

Chief Hawkwind guides the tribe's braves and coordinates the defenses of the mesa, alongside the tribe's revered elder, Greatmother Hawkwind. The tribe's trainers and elders gather at the center of the camp to instruct young adventurers.

The encampment is continually harassed by Bristleback quilboar operating out of Brambleblade Ravine to the east. In addition to feral battleboars and striders wandering the surrounding bluffs, the lingering danger of predatory centaur bands keeps the Hawkwind braves on constant alert.

Red Cloud Mesa is naturally bounded by sheer cliffs. The only way down into the greater plains of Mulgore is along a guarded mountain path leading north, watched over by Hawkwind braves to prevent hostile beasts and quilboar from ambushing travelers.

Coldridge Valley. Coldridge Valley is a sheltered, snow-covered vale tucked into the southwestern heights of Dun Morogh. Centered around the hamlet of Anvilmar, it serves as the training ground where young dwarves and gnome refugees first take up arms in service of Ironforge. A single tunnel, Coldridge Pass, connects this secluded hollow to the wider mountain realm. Cradled by sheer mountain cliffs, Coldridge Valley remains largely cut off from the bustling trade routes of Dun Morogh. At its heart sits Anvilmar, a sturdy stone hall and hamlet where veteran dwarven instructors and displaced gnome scholars train fresh recruits in the arts of battle, stealth, and sorcery. Outside the warmth of Anvilmar's hearths, the valley floor is carpeted in thick snow and prowled by boars and hungry winter wolves, providing novices with their first real taste of frontier survival.

The only overland route out of the valley leads through Coldridge Pass, a snowy tunnel cutting northeast through the mountain ridge. Once through the pass, the road heads east directly toward the town of Kharanos and onward to the great gates of Ironforge.

Following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan to troggs and radioactive fallout, surviving gnomes fled into Dun Morogh as refugees. High Tinker Mekkatorque's people were welcomed by King Magni Bronzebeard, leading many exiled gnomish apprentices to train side by side with young dwarves in Anvilmar.

The valley faces two major menaces: the hostile Frostmane trolls, who resent dwarven settlements on their mountain territory, and crude Rockjaw troggs, who have clawed up from the deep earth to choke Coldridge Pass. Local predators like wolves and boars also harass unwary travelers.

Anvilmar is the central fortress-lodge and settlement within Coldridge Valley. It houses class trainers, forge-masters, and local mountaineer officers who coordinate the defense of the valley and prepare newly forged adventurers for the wider world.

Deathknell. Deathknell is a fortified village nestled in a secluded valley in southwestern Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the primary awakening grounds for newly freed undead breaking free from the Lich King's grasp to join the Forsaken. Besieged by mindless Scourge remnants, local zealots, and aggressive wildlife, the settlement is a harsh proving ground for those claiming a place in Sylvanas Windrunner's kingdom. Tucked away behind jagged hills just north of the Silverpine border, Deathknell is where newly awakened undead first open their eyes to their bleak reality. Unlike most settlements in Tirisfal Glades that preserved their human names from the fallen Kingdom of Lordaeron, Deathknell was explicitly renamed by the undead who claimed it. The town itself is cleaved in two: the Forsaken cling stubbornly to the southern grounds around the old church, while the northern half—including the village forge—remains overrun by mindless Scourge zombies and feral ghouls. Elite Deathguards keep the narrow gorge out of the valley securely sealed against intruders, allowing local caretakers to induct new arrivals into the Banshee Queen's service.

While most settlements throughout Tirisfal Glades retained their human Lordaeron names, Deathknell is a notable exception. The Forsaken chose the moniker intentionally upon taking root in the valley, marking the site as both the death of their old human existence and the grim bell sounding their rebirth into undeath.

Not every corpse raised in the wake of the Third War broke free with their minds intact. The northern village square and forge are infested by the 'Mindless Ones'—feral zombies, ghouls, and skeletons still driven by the residual, lingering will of the Scourge. Forsaken defenders regularly clear them out to salvage equipment and defend the church.

A detachment of the Scarlet Crusade maintains an encampment in the hills southeast of the village. Fanatically dedicated to destroying all undead indiscriminately, they monitor the pass, ambush newly awakened Forsaken, and exchange scouting intelligence with Scarlet strongholds elsewhere in Lordaeron.

Night Web's Hollow, the gold mine situated in the cliffs northwest of the village, is completely overrun by aggressive spiders. Securing natural resources like gold is critical for the Forsaken war effort, but until the infestation is cleared, the settlement cannot exploit the vein.

Northshire Abbey. Northshire Abbey is a historic monastery nestled in Northshire Valley within the northern foothills of Elwynn Forest. Rebuilt after its destruction in the First War, it serves as the spiritual heart of the Brotherhood of Northshire and a premier training center for new defenders answering the kingdom of Stormwind's call. Centuries ago, clerics from Lordaeron traveled south into the kingdom of Stormwind to spread the worship of the Holy Light, establishing the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics and their abbey. The monastery quickly became an anchor of kingdom life, caring for the sick and even tending to the young Guardian Medivh during his years in a coma. During the First War, the abbey suffered repeated assaults by brigands and the Orcish Horde, culminating in its utter destruction. When the Alliance of Lordaeron liberated the region in the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped rebuild the sanctuary, refounding its protectors as the Brotherhood of Northshire.

The Brotherhood of Northshire is a religious order of clerics, priests, and paladins based out of Northshire Abbey. Originally founded centuries ago by missioning clerics from Lordaeron, it was re-established by Archbishop Alonsus Faol after the First War to train faithful defenders and preserve sacred scripture.

During the First War, the abbey held strategic and spiritual importance for Stormwind. Orcish forces incited human brigands to attack it, and after the half-orc Garona was briefly held captive there, a massive Horde onslaught leveled the holy grounds. It remained ruined throughout the war until the Alliance drove out the orcish clans and rebuilt it.

Stormwind's military is stretched thin protecting distant borders, leaving outlying regions poorly guarded. Opportunistic kobolds have infested the local gold mines, while the Defias Brotherhood exploits the gaps to rob travelers, harass the local vineyards, and raid the abbey's library for arcane tomes and holy relics.

During the First War, an ogre chieftain named Turok stole the sacred Tome of Divinity from Northshire Abbey and retreated into the Deadmines. Sir Anduin Lothar led an expedition into the depths to recover the holy scripture, getting trapped until a royal rescue party saved him and returned the tome to the abbey's care.

Sen'jin Village. Sen'jin Village is a coastal settlement on the southern shores of Durotar, serving as a sanctuary for the Darkspear trolls. Established by Chieftain Vol'jin after his people were driven from their ancestral home on the Echo Isles, the hamlet honors his fallen father, the witch doctor Sen'jin. Today, it stands as a fragile haven focused on survival, herbalism, and reclaiming what was stolen. When the dark witch doctor Zalazane betrayed the Darkspear and seized control of the Echo Isles, Chieftain Vol'jin was forced to lead the survivors across the strait to the mainland of Durotar. There, nestled beneath coastal cliffs and looking out over the water, they raised crude huts and established Sen'jin Village. The settlement carries the name of Vol'jin's father, the venerable elder who sacrificed himself during the Third War to save their people from coastal murlocs. Despite their close alliance with Thrall's Horde, the trolls here live under the shadow of exile, staring daily across the shallows at the home they lost.

Shadowglen. Shadowglen is a secluded, twilit vale nestled within the northeastern boughs of Teldrassil. Dominated by the great barrow-tree Aldrassil, it serves as the safe haven where young night elves take their first steps into service before journeying out into the wider world. Tucked away in the northeastern canopy of Teldrassil, Shadowglen is ringed by high ridges that shelter it from the rest of the world. Bathed in eternal dusk, the vale centers on Aldrassil, a massive barrow-tree whose hollowed trunk houses elders, priestesses, and mentors for young night elves beginning their training. The only route out of the valley leads south through a narrow mountain pass toward Starbreeze Village and Dolanaar, making Shadowglen one of the most naturally fortified and peaceful sanctuaries on the World Tree.

Shadowglen is the sheltered starting grove for the night elves, located in the northeastern reaches of Teldrassil. It is a peaceful, secluded haven centered around the grand tree Aldrassil, where novices train under mentors before journeying across the World Tree.

The tree is Aldrassil, a barrow-tree that forms the heart of Shadowglen. Its hollowed interior serves as an administrative lodge and training hub where novice night elves meet class trainers, mentors, and caretakers.

The primary threat comes from the northwest in Shadowthread Cave, a cavern infested with venomous spiders that regularly creep out into the glade. Young defenders are tasked with culling the spiders and calming the restless local wildlife.
Shadowglen is entirely surrounded by ridges except for a single path to the south. Passing through this narrow mountain gap leads southward toward Starbreeze Village and the settlement of Dolanaar.

Valley of Trials. Tucked away behind the rugged red cliffs of southern Durotar, the Valley of Trials serves as the testing ground for new recruits of the Horde. Young orcs and their Darkspear troll allies come here to prove their strength and earn their place among the warriors of Kalimdor. Those who survive the valley's harsh wildlife and hidden threats depart ready to defend their fledgling nation. The Valley of Trials is designed to weed out the weak before they ever set foot in the broader reaches of Durotar. Overseen by chieftains and trainers stationed in the carved cliffside shelter known as The Den, young fighters are thrust into the sun-scorched gulch to hunt scorpids, culled aggressive boars, and enforce discipline among lazy peons harvesting scarce timber. The trial is uncompromising: those who prove their mettle earn the right to venture forth as true soldiers of the Horde, while those who fail are left to bleach beneath the desert sun.

It is the traditional proving ground for recruits of the Horde, primarily young orcs and Darkspear trolls. Within its sheltered canyons, new adventurers complete rigorous tasks to demonstrate their martial skill, survival instinct, and loyalty before being permitted to leave for the rest of Durotar.

The Den is a cave carved into the cliffs roughly in the center of the valley. It houses class trainers, vendors, and overseers like Gornek who direct new recruits, equip them, and monitor their progress during their initial trials.

Cultists belonging to the Burning Blade have established a secret coven in the northern caves. Although trainers use their weak familiars to test recruits, the cult's presence suggests shadowy forces like the Shadow Council are seeking a foothold right on Durotar's doorsteps.

Sarkoth is an unusually large, venomous scorpid residing in the rocky heights of the valley. Due to his aggression and lethality, instructors task promising recruits with hunting him down to test their courage and bring back his mangled claw as proof.

Skyborne. The Skyborne, or shen'dorei, are an offshoot of high elves descended from rebels who fled Eldre'Thalas after opposing Prince Tortheldrin's demonic pacts. Striking a desperate bargain with wind spirits, their ancestors escaped Azeroth to dwell atop the floating Zephras Isle within Skywall. Today, with their elemental benefactors abruptly gone, their floating sanctuary faces internal fractures and physical collapse. Following the Sundering, the Shen'dralar of Eldre'Thalas languished without the Well of Eternity. Prince Tortheldrin devised a dark salvation: summon the demon Immol'thar and siphon its power. Horrified nobles and citizens resisted, fearing another Legion invasion. In response, Tortheldrin executed a bloody purge of dozens of houses. From the surviving shadows rose a resistance spearheaded by a masked figure known only as the Shal'nan ('the Veiled One'). When a desperate rebel raid on Tortheldrin's ritual sanctum descended into catastrophic chaotic magic, the Shal'nan rallied the survivors and fled west to the port of Eldre'narr, taking to the seas pursued by the Prince's fleet.

The Skyborne, or shen'dorei ('the hidden people'), are high elves descended from ancient night elves who rebelled against Prince Tortheldrin in Eldre'Thalas. To escape his vengeful fleet, they struck a pact with wind spirits, who relocated their island, Zephras Isle, into the Elemental Plane of Air.

Millennia in the Elemental Plane of Air have subtly reshaped their biology. A recent phenomenon known as the Sky-Touched Blessing causes an increasing proportion of children—now roughly three out of ten—to be born with blue skin. Scholars predict their ancestral night elf traits will soon be entirely supplanted.

The Shal'nan, or 'the Veiled One', was the masked leader who spearheaded the resistance against Prince Tortheldrin's demon summoning in Eldre'Thalas. After leading the survivors to safety in Skywall, he abdicated to establish a democratic council, serving his people until mysteriously vanishing centuries ago alongside their elemental benefactors.

Zephras Isle is held aloft within Skywall by magical pylons attuned to elemental power. When the wind spirits who maintained them abruptly disappeared centuries ago, the anchoring pylons began to fail. Portions of the landmass have broken off into the void, stranding survivors and driving displaced elves to banditry.

They are the two primary cultural factions of the Skyborne. The High Order descends from Highborne magisters and seeks to rebuild their crumbling society through disciplined arcane mastery. The Windshapers trace their roots to ordinary night elf citizens and revere the elemental and spiritual customs cultivated during their time in Skywall.

The Al'Aketh are a desperate cult of Skyborne who worship Al'Akir the Windlord. While their ancestors' elemental benefactors feared and avoided speaking of Al'Akir, the collapse of Zephras Isle led homeless and disenfranchised refugees to turn to the elemental lord for salvation and power.

Ashenvale. Ashenvale is the ancient, rain-drenched ancestral forest of the night elves, held sacred under the protection of the Sentinels and the demigod Cenarius. Bordering the Barrens to the south and Darkshore to the north, it has erupted into a bitter war zone as the Horde harvests timber to build its young nation. Ancient trees and tranquil moonwells share canopy with demonic holdouts, hostile beastmen, and clash points along the contested frontier. Stretching beneath Mount Hyjal, Ashenvale has stood for millennia under the stewardship of the kaldorei and the children of Cenarius. Immense trees knit together into a dense canopy that turns daily rain into a gentle mist and casts the forest floor in eternal twilight. Ancient ruins of elven civilization poke through the moss, guarded by walking ancients and dryads. For thousands of years, the night elves built no true cities here, preferring to hunt lightly and preserve the wild domain in pristine balance.

The Barrens. The Barrens is an expansive, sun-baked savanna that serves as the beating geographical and logistical heart of the Horde in central Kalimdor. Once a verdant forest prior to the Great Sundering, it is now an arid plain of red dust, hardy scrub, and wandering wildlife. Centered around the strategic hub of the Crossroads, the land remains locked in constant struggle against quilboar tribes, centaur raiders, and creeping corruption. For countless generations, nomadic tauren hunted kodo and zhevra across these plains while waging a defensive, cyclical war against marauding Kolkar centaur. When Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor during the Third War, he aided Cairne Bloodhoof in repelling the centaur and traversing the savanna into Mulgore. Today, the Barrens connects Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale. Outposts like the Crossroads and Camp Taurajo secure trade along the Gold Road, while orcish homesteads brave the arid climate to forge a lasting home.

Blackfathom Deeps. Blackfathom Deeps is a flooded subterranean temple complex situated along the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Once a shrine dedicated to the night elven moon goddess Elune, the sunken sanctuary has been overtaken by the Twilight's Hammer cult, treacherous naga, and satyrs. They gather in its dark waters to venerate and nurture Aku'mai, a primordial pet and herald of the Old Gods. Long before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, this complex was known as Lathar'Lazal, a splendid temple dedicated to Elune. Highborne masons raised gem-encrusted bridges while Queen Azshara commanded the surrounding waters, partitionining salt seas and mountain streams around a sacred moonwell. When the Sundering tore the world apart ten thousand years ago, the temple sank into the coastal depths of the Veiled Sea. For millenia, it sat undisturbed beneath the waves—until foul whispers began seeping upward from the subterranean dark.

Darkshore. Darkshore is a cold, mist-shrouded strip of coast lining northwestern Kalimdor, dotted with ancient Kaldorei ruins and troubled wildlife. Anchored by the Alliance harbor town of Auberdine, it serves as the primary continental gateway for travelers arriving from Teldrassil and the Eastern Kingdoms. Beyond the patrolled road, demonic cults, encroaching naga, and a creeping corruption from the highlands threaten the region's delicate balance. Stretching beneath the western shadows of Mount Hyjal and Felwood, Darkshore is characterized by pine groves, sea fog, and rocky beaches beaten by cold waves. Millennia ago, this coast was home to the flourishing Kaldorei twin cities of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran. Shattered during the Great Sundering, their skeletal pillars and marble arches now lie half-drowned in the surf or overgrown with roots, haunted by restless Highborne spirits and overrun by scavenger murlocs and invasive naga.

Darnassus. Darnassus is the serene, open-air capital city of the night elves, built amidst the branches of the newly planted World Tree, Teldrassil. Governed by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind alongside the druids of the Cenarion Enclave, it serves as a tranquil sanctuary for an ancient people adapting to mortality. Sheltered across vast terraces surrounding a crystalline lake, it stands as the heart of night elf society and their bridge to the Alliance. Unlike the dense masonry of Stormwind or the carved stone tunnels of Ironforge, Darnassus is broad, quiet, and intimately open to the wilderness. Formed upon the upper canopy of Teldrassil off northern Kalimdor's coast, the capital's graceful wooden structures and winding pathways encircle a tranquil central lake. Elegant bridges connect terraces dedicated to tradesmen, craftsmen, sentinels, and druids, creating an atmosphere that balances civic governance with profound reverence for nature.

Because Teldrassil is an island isolated off Kalimdor's northwest coast, travelers must reach Rut'theran Village at the foot of the tree by boat or flight. From the village docks, a glowing magical transport tentacle takes travelers directly up into the city boughs.

High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind rules Darnassus and the kaldorei from the grand Temple of the Moon. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave, acting as the de facto druidic authority while Malfurion Stormrage remains lost in the Emerald Dream.

Darnassus was founded shortly after the Third War. When the night elves sacrificed their immortality to defeat Archimonde at Mount Hyjal, Fandral Staghelm pushed to grow the new World Tree, Teldrassil, to reclaim their former state. Darnassus was carved into the boughs as their new refuge.

Malfurion Stormrage is missing, his spirit trapped within the Emerald Dream. In his absence, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm governs the druids of Teldrassil, while Tyrande Whisperwind continually seeks a way to awaken and recover her beloved mate.

The city is divided into specialized terraces. The Craftsmen's Terrace hosts gathering and tailoring disciplines along with an inn, while the Tradesmen's Terrace houses trade stalls and the Auction House. Blacksmithing and martial trainers reside on the Warrior's Terrace, and the city bank rests upon the central island of the Temple Gardens.

After the devastation of the Third War, the night elves faced mounting pressure from the Horde, particularly orcish logging expeditions into Ashenvale. Recognizing the need for allies against these incursions and other rising threats across Kalimdor, Darnassus opened diplomatic ties and joined the Grand Alliance.

The Deadmines. Deep beneath the dusty farm town of Moonbrook lies the Deadmines, an enormous subterranean complex that once supplied a third of Stormwind's gold reserves. Abandoned during the First War and long considered haunted, these labyrinthine tunnels have secretly been overtaken by the Defias Brotherhood as their ultimate staging ground. Here, Edwin VanCleef and his conscripted goblin engineers labor away from the eyes of the realm to build an engine of vengeance against the kingdom. Before the First War, the Deadmines were celebrated as the greatest gold-producing center in human lands, financing the prosperity of Stormwind. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom and razed the capital, the mines were hastily abandoned to the dark. During those turbulent years, legendary figures walked these depths: Sir Anduin Lothar was imprisoned by subterranean ogres for twenty months while recovering the sacred Tome of Divinity, and Warchief Blackhand's rebellious daughter Griselda fled into the lower passages alongside the ogre Turok before both met their ends. Believed to be cursed and populated only by shambling undead and lurking subterranean vermin, the depths lay untouched for decades.

Dun Morogh. Dun Morogh is a snow-swept mountain highland situated at the heart of Khaz Modan. It serves as the ancestral starting ground and shared homeland for the dwarves of Ironforge and the displaced gnomes of Gnomeregan. Though guarded by towering peaks and fortified passes, the snowy realm faces rising internal threats from troggs, Frostmane trolls, and irradiated leper gnomes. Dun Morogh occupies the highest peaks in the Eastern Kingdoms, an alpine expanse ringed by jagged summits that shield it from Searing Gorge to the south and the Wetlands to the north. These snowy mountains feed the rivers flowing across Khaz Modan and provide near-limitless veins of copper and iron. Access is heavily restricted to mountain tunnels like North Gate Pass and South Gate Pass, watched closely by dwarven Mountaineers. At the heart of the region sits Ironforge, an ancient subterranean wonder and the capital of King Magni Bronzebeard's realm, linked straight to Stormwind by the marvel of the Deeprun Tram.
Both dwarves and gnomes begin their journeys here in Coldridge Valley, a sheltered basin in southwestern Dun Morogh, before venturing out through Coldridge Pass into Kharanos and the wider zone.

During the Third War, a subterranean race called troggs swarmed Gnomeregan. In an attempt to purge the invaders, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque released radioactive gas into the lower levels. The plan failed catastrophically, killing thousands and irradiating many gnomes into crazed leper gnomes, forcing the healthy survivors to flee to Ironforge.

Dun Morogh is walled in by high mountain ridges. To travel eastward into Loch Modan on foot, take the roads leading to North Gate Pass or South Gate Pass in the northeastern mountains. You can also travel directly to Stormwind City via the Deeprun Tram inside Ironforge.

The only functional Alliance flight master in the zone is located inside the Great Forge of Ironforge, connecting travelers to locations across Khaz Modan, Stormwind, and the northern Alliance outposts.

The Frostmane are a tribe of ice trolls who ruled Dun Morogh long before the dwarves emerged from Uldaman. Though defeated and driven into the crags generations ago, they remain bitter enemies of Ironforge, routinely raiding dwarven farms and roads from retreats like Frostmane Hold.

Kharanos is the primary dwarven settlement in central Dun Morogh. It houses the Thunderbrew Distillery, trainers, and supplies, serving as the central operational hub for young adventurers and Mountaineers tackling local troll and wildlife problems.

Durotar. Durotar is the arid, red-rock homeland founded by Warchief Thrall following the Third War, named in honor of his father, Durotan. Bounded by the Southfury River and the Great Sea, it serves as the heartland of the New Horde and the proving ground for young orcs and Darkspear trolls. Within its harsh canyons lie fortified settlements like Razor Hill, the sprawling warrior city of Orgrimmar, and entrenched hostile holdouts ranging from quilboar tribes to stranded Alliance troops. When Thrall led his people across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, he deliberately sought an untamed frontier where the orcs could carve out an honest existence through labor and grit rather than conquest. Durotar's cracked red soil, baked gullies, and towering red-rock spires remind the orcs deeply of Draenor before its destruction. While the climate is unforgiving, offering little arable land and sparse water, the Horde embraced the landscape's natural defense and austere majesty. Bordered to the west across the Southfury River by the open Barrens and to the north by the ruined wilderness of Azshara, Durotar stands as living proof that the orcs have forged their own destiny.

Thrall chose this unforgiving territory intentionally. The red earth and rugged mesas reminded the orcs of their ancestral world of Draenor, while its harsh conditions served as penance and a forge for discipline. Thrall believed his people needed to earn their survival through honest hardship rather than claiming fertile lands by conquest, ensuring they would not slide back into bloodthirsty complacency.

The land was named in honor of Durotan, Thrall's late father and the former chieftain of the Frostwolf clan. Durotan had opposed the demonic corruption of the orcish clans and was murdered on the orders of the warlock Gul'dan.

The soldiers at Tiragarde Keep are surviving Kul Tiran marines under Lieutenant Benedict, left over from Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's invasion fleet. Even after Proudmoore was slain, these troops refused to surrender or withdraw, maintaining an entrenched hostile outpost right on Durotar's southern coast.

The Darkspear trolls originally established their Kalimdor home on the Echo Isles. However, a powerful witch doctor named Zalazane succumbed to madness and turned his dark magic against his brethren, enslaving their minds. The survivors fled to the mainland to establish Sen'jin Village, from which they launch raids to break his hold.

The Burning Blade is a subversive demonic cult loyal to the Shadow Council and the Burning Legion. Operatives lurk in secluded spots like Skull Rock and the Burning Blade Coven, attempting to undermine Thrall's leadership and tempt impressionable orcs back into demonic servitude.

A bridge over the Southfury River leads west into the Barrens, while a path through northern Orgrimmar crosses into Azshara. Outside Orgrimmar, twin zeppelin towers provide transcontinental air travel directly to Tirisfal Glades and Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale.

Duskwood. Once a sunlit expanse of southern Elwynn known as Brightwood, Duskwood is now a cursed woodland trapped beneath an unnatural, perpetual gloom. Abandoned by the authorities in Stormwind, its besieged human inhabitants cling to survival in Darkshire under the watchful protection of the local Night Watch militia. Across its darkened groves and haunted barrows roam flesh-eating ghouls, gigantic venomous spiders, raiding ogres, and savage, mysterious worgen. Before the darkness descended, this province was known as Brightwood, a rich agricultural tract of the Kingdom of Stormwind boasting prosperous settlements like Grand Hamlet and Raven Hill. The region's tragedy began when Guardian Medivh fell at Karazhan during the First War, unleashing waves of corrupted fel magic that twisted the serene woodland into a gnarled, shadowy morass. Spiders mutated into terrifying predatory beasts, while fleeing wolves spilled north into Elwynn Forest. Over time, Grand Hamlet was rechristened Darkshire, its terrified townsfolk left largely to fend for themselves as the realm's royal garrison withdrew to defend the capital.

Elwynn Forest. Elwynn Forest is the verdant heartland of the Kingdom of Stormwind, providing the capital with essential timber, gold, fish, and crops. Sheltered beneath stately hardwoods, it serves as the proving ground for new human recruits stepping forth from Northshire Abbey. Yet beneath its idyllic pastoral canopy, the woods are sorely beleaguered by encroaching vermin, displaced wildlife, and widespread brigandage. Stretching south from the gates of Stormwind down to the Nazferiti River, Elwynn is a fertile region blessed with abundant rainfall and dense hardwood forests. Communities like Goldshire and the Eastvale Logging Camp provide crucial grain, livestock, lumber, and raw copper to sustain the grand capital. The region is also celebrated for breeding sturdy Evendale horses, favored by travelers and knights across the kingdom.

Stormwind's armed forces are severely overstretched. The kingdom expanded heavy military deployments southward into Stranglethorn Vale, running up deep debts and draining local manpower. As a result, outposts like Westbrook Garrison and Goldshire rely on small skeleton crews and volunteer recruits to fight off bandits, gnolls, and murlocs.

With guards in short supply, opportunistic kobolds swarmed into Fargodeep Mine, Jasperlode Mine, and Echo Ridge Mine in search of precious gold and minerals. They drove out the human prospectors and miners, aggressively defending their subterranean claims with candles, crude picks, and scavenged tools.

They are members of the Defias Brotherhood, led by Edwin VanCleef. Many were originally artisans of the Stonemasons Guild who rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War. When the nobility refused to pay them their promised wages, riots broke out, leading to their banishment and descent into organized brigandage.

Crossing the bridge over the Nazferiti River takes you into Duskwood, historically known as Brightwood. That once-peaceful territory has fallen into unnatural darkness and is now infested with undead, monstrous spiders, and ravenous beasts.

The Stonefields and the Maclures are neighboring farming families in southern Elwynn who have maintained a bitter, longstanding grudge against each other. Despite their endless bickering and accusations, two of their younger kin—Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield—have secretly fallen in love, complicating the rivalry even further.

The Tower of Azora is an arcane spire located along the road between Goldshire and the Eastvale Logging Camp. It houses secluded mages, including Theocritus, who observe the region's leylines and conduct magical research outside the direct oversight of Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum.

Gnomeregan. Carved into the snowy foothills of Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan was once the subterranean capital and greatest technological wonder of the gnomish race. Today it lies ruined and quarantined, poisoned by radioactive fallout following a desperate defense against an underground trogg invasion. Its surviving people now dwell as refugees in nearby Ironforge, while the irradiated halls remain overrun by mutated troggs, deranged leper gnomes, and rogue mechanical sentries. Long before its tragic fall, Gnomeregan stood as a testament to the heights of gnomish brilliance, ambition, and industry. Constructed with the assistance of the nearby dwarves of Ironforge, the sprawling mechanical complex was powered by giant grinding engines, whirring gears, and an intricate ventilation network that required fifteen technicians working around the clock just to maintain fresh air. It was a thriving center of invention, competitive craft, and politics centered on Tinkers' Court, serving as the proud capital from which gnomes contributed invaluable siege engines, flying machines, and armaments to the Alliance of Lordaeron during the Second War.

Hall of Thanes. Deep beneath the bustling city of Ironforge lies the Hall of Thanes, an ancient subterranean complex steeped in dwarven history. Intended for early Alliance adventurers, this secluded dungeon holds relics of the mountain kingdom's past that have fallen into peril. Gaining entry requires unearthing forgotten routes through the mountain itself. While Ironforge hums with the ringing of hammers in the Great Forge, forgotten halls delve far deeper beneath the stone. The Hall of Thanes represents one of these venerable subterranean reaches. Long tied to ancestral dwarven bloodlines and relics of stonecraft, it now requires intrepid Alliance champions to venture into its shadowed vaults to secure the depths.

Hillsbrad Foothills. Hillsbrad Foothills is a green, fertile region that represents the last pastoral bastion of the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron. Despite having largely escaped the Scourge's plague, the land is torn apart by brutal open war between the humans of Southshore and the Forsaken entrenched at Tarren Mill. It serves as a violent crossroads where the armies of the Alliance and the Horde clash without mercy. While northern Lordaeron rots under the blight of the Scourge, Hillsbrad remains strikingly green. Its rolling pastures, pine groves, and working farmsteads offer travelers a rare glimpse of what the kingdom looked like before the Third War. Yet that tranquil appearance is deceptive. The peaceful fields and rural roads are constantly swept by armed patrols, rogue mercenaries, and scavenger beasts. What should be Lordaeron's breadbasket has instead become its most contested borderland.

Ironforge. Carved into the heart of Ironforge Mountain in snowy Dun Morogh, Ironforge is the ancestral capital of the Bronzebeard dwarves and an unassailable bastion of the Alliance. Centered on the molten heat of the Great Forge, this sprawling underground city serves as a bustling hub of commerce, industry, and ancient dwarven lore. Under the steadfast rule of King Magni Bronzebeard, it now also shelters the displaced gnomes of nearby Gnomeregan. Ironforge was founded twenty-five hundred years ago when the first generation of dwarves awakened in Uldaman and journeyed west into Dun Morogh's jagged peaks. Delving into the tallest mountain, they built a massive shrine to their titan progenitor Khaz'goroth alongside the colossal Great Forge. Ever since, the city has expanded in concentric rings around that fiery hearth. Unlike surface capitals, Ironforge is entirely enclosed beneath stone ceilings, warmed by roaring hearths and subterranean rivers of molten magma. Its fortified gates and cavernous depths have proven near-impregnable throughout centuries of war.

King Magni Bronzebeard rules Ironforge and the kingdom of Khaz Modan from the High Seat. A skilled warrior and master blacksmith, he has governed his people through the Second and Third Wars and remains a deeply loyal pillar of the Alliance.

When the nearby gnomish capital of Gnomeregan fell to a sudden trogg invasion and a disastrous radiation accident, the surviving gnomes fled into Dun Morogh. King Magni welcomed them into Ironforge, granting them an entire quarter of the city now known as Tinker Town.

The Great Forge is the fiery industrial heart of the city, fed by underground waterfalls of molten magma. It surrounds the Great Anvil, where dwarven weaponsmiths craft legendary arms and armor. King Magni himself forged the famed holy blade Ashbringer upon this anvil.

Ironforge is connected directly to Stormwind City by the Deeprun Tram, an extraordinary subterranean railway built by gnomish engineering that cuts straight through the mountain bedrock of the Eastern Kingdoms.

Ironforge has never fallen to an outside invader. Kilrogg Deadeye's Bleeding Hollow clan laid siege to it for months during the Second War, and the Dark Irons fought into the city during the War of the Three Hammers, but the gates and defenders held.

After the War of the Three Hammers, the defeated Wildhammer clan relocated north into the Wetlands and the Hinterlands, while the hostile Dark Iron clan settled within the Redridge and Blackrock regions under the thrall of the Firelord.

Loch Modan. Loch Modan is a temperate mountain valley east of Dun Morogh, renowned for its massive alpine lake held in place by the monumental Stonewrought Dam.
